text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. The heart of CI is the automated build process. Every time a developer pushes new code, a CI pipeline is triggered. This pipeline automatically compiles the entire project and runs a full suite of tests. The main advantage of this approach is catching issues early. Instead of discovering a broken feature weeks later, the team gets immediate feedback. If a test fails, the developer knows right away and can fix the problem before it becomes bigger. This practice keeps the software stable and makes collaboration much smoother.
